passage: *The Apricot Season* is a novel. In the novel, the narrator describes her younger brother, Jasur, as a boy who cannot bear to wait for anything.
stem: Which quotation from *The Apricot Season* most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “Jasur was the tallest boy on our street, though he was only nine years old.”
option_b: “When Mother said the bread needed ten more minutes in the oven, Jasur sat down by the oven door and asked every few seconds whether the ten minutes were over yet.”
option_c: “Every summer, Jasur and I slept on the flat roof and counted the stars that fell across the sky.”
option_d: “Jasur kept a jar of river stones under his bed and could tell you exactly where he had found each one.”
explanation_en:
The claim is that Jasur cannot bear to wait. Choice B shows this directly: told to wait ten minutes, he sits by the oven and asks "every few seconds" whether the time is up.

Choice A describes his height, not his impatience. Choice C describes a summer habit he shares with the narrator. Choice D shows a careful collecting hobby, which, if anything, suggests patience rather than impatience.
explanation_uz:
Da’voga ko‘ra, Jasur hech narsani kutishga toqat qilolmaydi. B javob buni bevosita ko‘rsatadi: o‘n daqiqa kutish kerakligini eshitib, u tandir yonida o‘tirib oladi va "har bir necha soniyada" vaqt tugadimi, deb so‘raydi.

A uning bo‘yini tasvirlaydi, sabrsizligini emas. C hikoyachi bilan birga yozda qiladigan odatini tasvirlaydi. D tosh yig‘ishdek sinchkov mashg‘ulotni ko‘rsatadi, bu esa sabrsizlikdan ko‘ra sabrlilikka ishora qiladi.

passage: “Salt Flat at Noon” is a poem. In the poem, the speaker crosses a vast salt flat on foot and expresses a feeling of being very small in an enormous, empty landscape.
stem: Which quotation from “Salt Flat at Noon” most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “The salt cracks into tiles beneath my boots, / each one a careless, almost perfect shape.”
option_b: “Here the white ground runs past every edge of seeing, / and I am one dark stitch upon a sheet no hand could fold.”
option_c: “I filled my bottle at the last town's well / and did not think to fill a second one.”
option_d: “By evening I will reach the road again / and find the truck where I had left it parked.”
explanation_en:
The claim is that the speaker feels very small in a huge, empty landscape. Choice B presents the ground stretching "past every edge of seeing" and the speaker as a single "dark stitch" on an enormous sheet, an image of smallness within vastness.

Choice A describes the texture of the ground but not the speaker's size. Choice C mentions a practical mistake about water. Choice D looks ahead to leaving the salt flat and says nothing about feeling small.
explanation_uz:
Da’voga ko‘ra, so‘zlovchi ulkan va bo‘m-bo‘sh manzara ichida o‘zini juda kichik his qiladi. B javobda yer "ko‘z yetgan har bir chegaradan nariga" cho‘zilgan, so‘zlovchi esa ulkan choyshabdagi bitta "qora chok" sifatida tasvirlangan: bu kenglik ichidagi kichiklik obrazi.

A yerning ko‘rinishini tasvirlaydi, lekin so‘zlovchining kichikligi haqida emas. C suv bilan bog‘liq amaliy xatoni eslatadi. D sho‘rxokdan chiqib ketishni o‘ylaydi va o‘zini kichik his qilish haqida hech narsa demaydi.

passage: Many plants in dry regions have features that limit water loss. Botanist Malika Ergasheva studies a desert shrub whose leaves are covered with a thick, waxy coating. She hypothesizes that the coating helps the shrub conserve water by reducing the amount of water that evaporates through the surface of its leaves.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ergasheva's hypothesis?
option_a: Leaves from which the waxy coating had been carefully removed lost water much faster than untreated leaves from the same shrubs.
option_b: The waxy coating is thicker on the shrub's older leaves than on its younger leaves.
option_c: The shrub produces small yellow flowers only in years with above-average rainfall.
option_d: Several insects that feed on the shrub avoid leaves with especially thick coatings.
explanation_en:
Ergasheva's hypothesis is that the coating reduces water loss from the leaves. Choice A shows that removing the coating makes the leaves lose water much faster, which is exactly what the hypothesis predicts.

Choice B describes where the coating is thicker but does not connect the coating to water loss. Choice C is about flowering and rainfall, not the coating. Choice D suggests the coating may protect against insects, a different function from the one Ergasheva proposes.
explanation_uz:
Ergashevaning farazi shuki, mumsimon qoplama barglardan suv yo‘qotilishini kamaytiradi. A javob qoplama olib tashlansa, barglar suvni ancha tez yo‘qotishini ko‘rsatadi, bu aynan faraz kutgan natija.

B qoplama qayerda qalinroq ekanini aytadi, lekin uni suv yo‘qotish bilan bog‘lamaydi. C qoplama haqida emas, gullash va yog‘ingarchilik haqida. D qoplama hasharotlardan himoya qilishi mumkinligini ko‘rsatadi, bu Ergasheva taklif qilgan vazifadan boshqa vazifa.

passage: At a weekly farmers' market, some sellers label their fruit with a price per kilogram, while others give a price per piece. Economist Bobur Karimov hypothesizes that shoppers buy more fruit when prices are shown per piece, because a price per piece is easier to understand at a glance.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Karimov's hypothesis?
option_a: Most shoppers at the market said that they visit it at least once a week.
option_b: Fruit prices at the market rose slightly over the course of the study.
option_c: Sellers of vegetables at the market used per-kilogram labels throughout the study.
option_d: When the same sellers switched between the two kinds of labels on alternating weeks, their fruit sales were consistently higher in the weeks with per-piece labels.
explanation_en:
Karimov predicts that per-piece prices lead shoppers to buy more fruit. Choice D compares the same sellers using each kind of label and finds higher sales with per-piece labels, which directly supports the hypothesis.

Choice A describes how often shoppers visit but not how labels affect buying. Choice B notes a general price change that is unrelated to the type of label. Choice C concerns vegetable sellers, who used only one kind of label, so it offers no comparison.
explanation_uz:
Karimovning taxminicha, dona narxi ko‘rsatilganda xaridorlar ko‘proq meva sotib oladi. D javob bir xil sotuvchilarni ikkala yorliq turi bilan solishtiradi va dona narxli yorliqlarda savdo yuqoriroq bo‘lganini ko‘rsatadi; bu farazni bevosita qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi.

A xaridorlar bozorga qanchalik tez-tez kelishini aytadi, yorliqlarning xaridga ta’sirini emas. B yorliq turiga aloqasi bo‘lmagan umumiy narx o‘zgarishini qayd etadi. C faqat bitta yorliq turidan foydalangan sabzavot sotuvchilari haqida, shuning uchun hech qanday solishtirish bermaydi.

passage: Ecologist Timur Saidov studies a species of tree frog whose skin is bright orange. Saidov hypothesizes that the color serves as a warning: it signals to birds and other predators that the frog tastes bad, so predators learn to leave it alone.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Saidov's hypothesis?
option_a: Birds in the frogs' habitat attacked clay frog models painted orange just as often as clay frog models painted brown.
option_b: The frog's skin contains chemicals that make it unpleasant for predators to eat.
option_c: Young frogs of the species turn orange only several weeks after they hatch.
option_d: Orange frogs of the species are found more often on leaves than on tree trunks.
explanation_en:
If the orange color warns predators away, birds should avoid orange models more than brown ones. Choice A shows that birds attacked orange and brown models equally often, so the color does not seem to protect the frog. This weakens Saidov's hypothesis.

Choice B shows that the frog really is unpleasant to eat, which fits the hypothesis. Choice C describes when the color develops but says nothing about how predators respond to it. Choice D describes where the frogs are found, which does not test the warning idea.
explanation_uz:
Agar to‘q sariq rang yirtqichlarni ogohlantirsa, qushlar to‘q sariq maketlardan jigarrang maketlarga qaraganda ko‘proq qochishi kerak. A javob qushlar ikkala rangdagi maketlarga bir xil tez-tez hujum qilganini ko‘rsatadi, ya’ni rang baqani himoya qilmayapti. Bu Saidovning farazini zaiflashtiradi.

B baqaning haqiqatan ham yoqimsiz ta’mga ega ekanini ko‘rsatadi, bu farazga mos. C rang qachon paydo bo‘lishini aytadi, yirtqichlar unga qanday munosabatda bo‘lishini emas. D baqalar qayerda uchrashini tasvirlaydi va ogohlantirish g‘oyasini sinamaydi.

passage: In a 2021 essay, architect Lola Yunusova argues that the traditional courtyard houses of her city were designed to keep the people living in them cool during hot summers without the help of any machines.
stem: Which quotation from Yunusova's essay most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “Many courtyard houses were built by large families who lived in them together for generations.”
option_b: “Today, a number of these houses have been turned into small hotels for visitors.”
option_c: “The high walls shade the courtyard for most of the day, and the small pool at its center cools the air that drifts into the surrounding rooms.”
option_d: “The carved wooden doors of the houses often show the initials of the families who first owned them.”
explanation_en:
Yunusova claims that the houses were designed to stay cool without machines. Choice C names two design features, shading walls and a central pool, and explains how they cool the rooms.

Choice A is about who lived in the houses, not how they stayed cool. Choice B describes how the houses are used today. Choice D describes decoration on the doors, which has nothing to do with cooling.
explanation_uz:
Yunusovaning fikricha, bu uylar mashinalarsiz salqin bo‘lib turadigan qilib loyihalangan. C javob ikki loyiha xususiyatini — soya beruvchi baland devorlar va o‘rtadagi hovuzni — nomlaydi va ular xonalarni qanday salqinlatishini tushuntiradi.

A uylarni qanday salqin saqlash haqida emas, ularda kim yashagani haqida. B uylardan bugun qanday foydalanilishini tasvirlaydi. D eshiklardagi bezakni tasvirlaydi, bu salqinlik bilan bog‘liq emas.

passage: *The Lamplighter's Daughter* is a play. In the play, Feruza tries to hide her disappointment from her family after learning that she was not accepted to a music school in the capital.
stem: Which quotation from *The Lamplighter's Daughter* most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “FERUZA: Mother, have you seen my blue scarf? I left it on this chair this morning.”
option_b: “FERUZA (laughing): You should have seen the baker's face when his cart tipped over in the street!”
option_c: “FERUZA (throwing the letter onto the table): They didn't even listen to me play! How could they say no?”
option_d: “FERUZA (smiling brightly, though her hands tremble as she folds the letter): Not accepted? Good. I never really wanted to move to the capital anyway.”
explanation_en:
The claim is that Feruza hides her disappointment. In Choice D, she smiles and claims she never wanted to go, but her trembling hands show the disappointment she is trying to hide.

Choice A is an ordinary question about a scarf. Choice B shows Feruza amused by an unrelated event. Choice C shows her disappointment openly, so it does not illustrate her hiding it.
explanation_uz:
Da’voga ko‘ra, Feruza umidsizligini oilasidan yashirishga harakat qiladi. D javobda u jilmayib, aslida poytaxtga ketishni xohlamaganini aytadi, ammo titrayotgan qo‘llari u yashirmoqchi bo‘lgan umidsizlikni fosh qiladi.

A ro‘mol haqidagi oddiy savol. B Feruzaning aloqasiz voqeadan kulayotganini ko‘rsatadi. C uning umidsizligini ochiq ko‘rsatadi, shuning uchun yashirishni misol qilmaydi.

passage: Astronomers have noticed that a distant star dims by about 20 percent for several days roughly every 140 days, then returns to its normal brightness. Astronomer Nodira Pulatova hypothesizes that a large cloud of dust orbits the star and blocks some of its light each time the cloud passes between the star and Earth.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Pulatova's hypothesis?
option_a: The star is about twice as massive as the Sun.
option_b: Other stars in the same region of the sky do not dim on a regular schedule.
option_c: The star's dimming has been recorded ever since astronomers first began observing it.
option_d: Observations with an infrared telescope detected a cloud of warm dust that orbits the star once every 140 days.
explanation_en:
Pulatova proposes that an orbiting dust cloud causes the regular dimming. Choice D reports a dust cloud that orbits the star on the same 140-day schedule as the dimming, which strongly supports her explanation.

Choice A gives the star's mass but does not connect it to dust or dimming. Choice B shows that the dimming is unusual but does not point to dust as its cause. Choice C shows how long the dimming has been observed, not what causes it.
explanation_uz:
Pulatova muntazam xiralashishga yulduz atrofida aylanadigan chang buluti sabab, deb taxmin qiladi. D javob yulduz atrofida xiralashish bilan bir xil — 140 kunlik — davr bilan aylanadigan chang buluti topilganini aytadi, bu uning tushuntirishini kuchli qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi.

A yulduzning massasini beradi, lekin uni chang yoki xiralashish bilan bog‘lamaydi. B xiralashish g‘ayrioddiy ekanini ko‘rsatadi, ammo uning sababi chang ekaniga ishora qilmaydi. C xiralashish qancha vaqtdan beri kuzatilayotganini aytadi, sababini emas.

passage: Twelve small portraits were recently discovered in a family archive. None of them is signed, and the archive contains no record of who painted them. Art historian Sherzod Abdullayev hypothesizes that a single artist painted all twelve portraits.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Abdullayev's hypothesis?
option_a: The twelve portraits show members of at least three different families.
option_b: Several of the portraits were damaged by water and later repaired.
option_c: Microscope images reveal the same unusual brushstroke pattern, a set of tiny crisscrossing lines, in the backgrounds of all twelve portraits.
option_d: Portraits painted in the same period and found in other archives are generally larger than these twelve.
explanation_en:
If one artist painted all twelve portraits, they should share that artist's personal technique. Choice C shows an unusual brushstroke pattern present in every portrait, which directly supports a single artist.

Choice A is about the people shown, and one artist could paint several families or several artists could paint one. Choice B describes later damage and repair, not the original painter. Choice D compares these portraits with others but says nothing about whether the twelve share one painter.
explanation_uz:
Agar o‘n ikki portretning hammasini bitta rassom chizgan bo‘lsa, ularda o‘sha rassomning shaxsiy uslubi takrorlanishi kerak. C javob har bir portretda bir xil g‘ayrioddiy mo‘yqalam izi borligini ko‘rsatadi, bu bitta rassom farazini bevosita qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi.

A tasvirlangan odamlar haqida: bitta rassom bir necha oilani, bir necha rassom esa bitta oilani chizishi mumkin. B keyingi shikast va ta’mir haqida, asl rassom haqida emas. D bu portretlarni boshqalari bilan solishtiradi, lekin o‘n ikkitasini bitta rassom chizganmi-yo‘qmi, buni aytmaydi.

passage: Last year, a school started an after-school reading club that meets twice a week. By the end of the year, the reading test scores of students in the club had risen noticeably. Principal Dilshod Rahimov concludes that the club caused the improvement.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Rahimov's conclusion?
option_a: Students in the club said that they enjoyed the books chosen for it.
option_b: The club met for the entire school year, including during exam periods.
option_c: Students at the school who did not join the club improved their reading test scores by the same amount over the same year.
option_d: Students who attended the most club meetings improved their scores the most.
explanation_en:
If the club caused the improvement, club members should have improved more than students who were not in the club. Choice C shows that nonmembers improved by the same amount, suggesting that something else, affecting all students, caused the rise. This weakens Rahimov's conclusion.

Choice A shows that students liked the club but not that it raised their scores. Choice B describes the club's schedule. Choice D links more club attendance to more improvement, which supports Rahimov's conclusion rather than weakening it.
explanation_uz:
Agar to‘garak natijalarni yaxshilagan bo‘lsa, uning a’zolari a’zo bo‘lmagan o‘quvchilardan ko‘proq o‘sishi kerak edi. C javob a’zo bo‘lmaganlar ham xuddi shuncha o‘sganini ko‘rsatadi, ya’ni o‘sishga barcha o‘quvchilarga ta’sir qilgan boshqa narsa sabab bo‘lgan. Bu Rahimovning xulosasini zaiflashtiradi.

A o‘quvchilarga to‘garak yoqqanini ko‘rsatadi, lekin u ballarni oshirganini emas. B to‘garak jadvalini tasvirlaydi. D ko‘proq qatnashish ko‘proq o‘sish bilan bog‘liqligini ko‘rsatadi, bu xulosani zaiflashtirmaydi, aksincha qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi.

passage: Beavers build dams that turn sections of fast-flowing streams into slow, still ponds. Ecologist Aziz Jo‘rayev hypothesizes that these ponds increase the variety of insects living along a stream, because the still water offers habitats that fast-flowing water does not.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Jo‘rayev's hypothesis?
option_a: The beaver dams in the study area were, on average, about one meter tall.
option_b: Stream sections with beaver ponds were home to more insect species than nearby sections of the same streams that had no ponds.
option_c: Some of the insect species found along the streams are eaten by fish.
option_d: All of the streams in the study were located at similar elevations.
explanation_en:
Jo‘rayev predicts that beaver ponds increase the number of insect species. Choice B compares sections of the same streams with and without ponds and finds more insect species where there are ponds, directly supporting the hypothesis.

Choice A describes the size of the dams, not their effect on insects. Choice C is about what eats the insects, not how many kinds there are. Choice D describes the study streams but gives no result about insects.
explanation_uz:
Jo‘rayevning taxminicha, qunduz hovuzlari hasharot turlari sonini ko‘paytiradi. B javob bir xil soylarning hovuzli va hovuzsiz qismlarini solishtiradi va hovuzli joylarda hasharot turlari ko‘proq ekanini ko‘rsatadi; bu farazni bevosita qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi.

A to‘g‘onlarning o‘lchamini tasvirlaydi, ularning hasharotlarga ta’sirini emas. C hasharotlarni kim yeyishi haqida, ularning nechta turi borligi haqida emas. D tadqiqotdagi soylarni tasvirlaydi, ammo hasharotlar haqida natija bermaydi.

passage: “The Glassblower's Apprentice” is a short story. In the story, the narrator, a young apprentice, becomes steadily more confident in his craft over the course of a year.
stem: Which quotation from “The Glassblower's Apprentice” most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “In my first month I shattered nearly every vase I touched; by spring I could shape a pitcher with my eyes half closed and hum while I worked.”
option_b: “The workshop smelled of smoke and hot sand from morning until night.”
option_c: “Master Halim rarely spoke, but when he did, every worker in the room stopped to listen.”
option_d: “I still remember the first vase I broke and how the pieces scattered across the floor like startled birds.”
explanation_en:
The claim describes a change over time: the apprentice grows more confident. Choice A contrasts his clumsy first month with his ease by spring, when he can work "with my eyes half closed," showing that growth.

Choice B describes the workshop. Choice C describes the master, not the apprentice's progress. Choice D recalls only an early failure and shows no later confidence.
explanation_uz:
Da’vo vaqt o‘tishi bilan bo‘ladigan o‘zgarishni tasvirlaydi: shogird tobora ishonchli bo‘lib boradi. A javob uning birinchi oydagi qo‘polligini bahordagi yengilligi bilan — "ko‘zlarimni yarim yumib" ishlay olishi bilan — taqqoslaydi va shu o‘sishni ko‘rsatadi.

B ustaxonani tasvirlaydi. C shogirdning rivojini emas, ustani tasvirlaydi. D faqat dastlabki muvaffaqiyatsizlikni eslaydi va keyingi ishonchni ko‘rsatmaydi.

passage: *The Weight of Wool* is a novel. In the novel, the narrator describes her father as both proud of the family's sheep farm and worried about its future.
stem: Which quotation from *The Weight of Wool* most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “Father had built the stone barn himself, carrying every rock up from the riverbed on his own back.”
option_b: “Father would lean on the fence each evening and declare that no flock in the valley could match ours, and then, almost in the same breath, wonder aloud how many more dry summers the pastures could survive.”
option_c: “When the rains failed for a third year, Father began selling the oldest sheep at the market in town.”
option_d: “Father rarely spoke at dinner, preferring to listen to my brothers argue about which of them could shear a sheep fastest.”
explanation_en:
The claim has two parts: the father is proud of the farm and worried about its future. Choice B shows both in a single moment: he boasts that no flock can match theirs, then wonders how many more dry summers the pastures can survive.

Choice A may suggest pride in his hard work but shows no worry. Choice C suggests worry about drought but shows no pride. Choice D shows that he is quiet at dinner and reveals neither feeling about the farm.
explanation_uz:
Da’vo ikki qismdan iborat: ota fermasidan faxrlanadi va uning kelajagidan xavotirda. B javob ikkalasini bir lahzada ko‘rsatadi: u vodiydagi hech bir suruv ularnikiga teng kelolmasligini aytib maqtanadi, so‘ng yaylovlar yana nechta qurg‘oqchil yozga chidashini o‘ylaydi.

A uning mehnatidan faxrlanishiga ishora qilishi mumkin, ammo xavotirni ko‘rsatmaydi. C qurg‘oqchilikdan xavotirga ishora qiladi, ammo faxrni ko‘rsatmaydi. D uning dasturxon atrofida jim o‘tirishini ko‘rsatadi va fermaga nisbatan hech bir tuyg‘uni ochib bermaydi.

passage: “Letter to the House on Plum Street” is a poem. In the poem, the speaker addresses the house where she grew up and suggests that, although she still misses it, she accepts that she can never return to live there.
stem: Which quotation from “Letter to the House on Plum Street” most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “I keep your key on the ring beside my own, / though I have learned no door is waiting for it.”
option_b: “Your kitchen windows always caught the morning first; / we ate our bread in squares of yellow light.”
option_c: “I will come back, I tell myself, next spring, / and climb your stairs as if no years had passed.”
option_d: “The new owners painted all your shutters green / and cut the walnut down to widen the drive.”
explanation_en:
The claim has two parts: the speaker still misses the house, and she accepts that she cannot return. In Choice A, keeping the old key shows that she still holds on to the house, while admitting that "no door is waiting for it" shows her acceptance.

Choice B shows fond memory but no acceptance. Choice C reverses the claim: the speaker expects to return. Choice D describes changes made by the new owners without showing either the speaker's longing or her acceptance.
explanation_uz:
Da’vo ikki qismdan iborat: so‘zlovchi uyni hali ham sog‘inadi va unga qaytib bo‘lmasligini tan oladi. A javobda eski kalitni saqlab yurishi uning uyga hali ham bog‘liqligini, "uni hech bir eshik kutmayotganini" tan olishi esa bu haqiqatni qabul qilganini ko‘rsatadi.

B iliq xotirani ko‘rsatadi, lekin qabul qilishni emas. C da’voga teskari: so‘zlovchi qaytishni kutmoqda. D yangi egalar kiritgan o‘zgarishlarni tasvirlaydi va na sog‘inchni, na qabul qilishni ko‘rsatadi.

passage: A range of low hills in a dry region contains thick layers of smooth, rounded pebbles. Pebbles become rounded when they are tumbled against one another over long distances. Geologist Kamola Sharipova hypothesizes that the pebbles were carried to the hills and deposited there by a large river that flowed through the region millions of years ago.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Sharipova's hypothesis?
option_a: The pebbles are made of types of rock found only in mountains more than 200 kilometers away, at the far end of an ancient, now-dry valley that leads directly to the hills.
option_b: The hills are higher at their northern end than at their southern end.
option_c: The pebble layers are covered by a thin layer of windblown sand.
option_d: Similar layers of rounded pebbles have been found in several other dry regions of the world.
explanation_en:
Sharipova proposes that an ancient river carried the pebbles a long way to the hills. Choice A shows that the pebbles came from distant mountains connected to the hills by an ancient valley, the kind of path a river would follow. This fits the hypothesis closely.

Choice B describes the shape of the hills but not the pebbles' origin. Choice C describes material deposited on top of the pebbles, probably by wind, which says nothing about how the pebbles arrived. Choice D shows that such layers exist elsewhere but gives no evidence about a river in this region.
explanation_uz:
Sharipovaning farazicha, qadimgi daryo toshlarni uzoq masofadan tepaliklarga olib kelgan. A javob toshlar tepaliklar bilan qadimiy vodiy orqali bog‘langan uzoq tog‘lardan kelganini ko‘rsatadi, daryo aynan shunday yo‘ldan oqadi. Bu farazga juda mos.

B tepaliklarning shaklini tasvirlaydi, toshlarning kelib chiqishini emas. C toshlar ustiga, ehtimol shamol olib kelgan qatlamni tasvirlaydi va toshlar qanday kelganini aytmaydi. D bunday qatlamlar boshqa joylarda ham borligini ko‘rsatadi, lekin aynan shu hududdagi daryo haqida dalil bermaydi.

passage: At a hilltop site, archaeologists uncovered a set of large clay storage jars from about 3,000 years ago. Archaeologist Behzod Tursunov argues that the jars were made at the site itself rather than brought there from somewhere else.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Tursunov's argument?
option_a: Pieces of a kiln that was used for firing pottery were found at the site.
option_b: The jars are decorated with patterns that also appear on other pottery found at the site.
option_c: Chemical analysis shows that the clay in the jars matches clay from a riverbank 300 kilometers away and differs from every clay source within 50 kilometers of the site.
option_d: The jars were found together in a single room near the site's main gate.
explanation_en:
Tursunov argues that the jars were made locally. Choice C shows that their clay came from a distant riverbank and matches no nearby source, which suggests that the jars were made elsewhere. This weakens his argument.

Choice A shows that pottery was made at the site, which supports Tursunov. Choice B links the jars to local pottery, which also supports him. Choice D tells where the jars were found, not where they were made.
explanation_uz:
Tursunov idishlar shu joyning o‘zida yasalgan, deb ta’kidlaydi. C javob ularning loyi uzoqdagi daryo qirg‘og‘idan olinganini va yaqin atrofdagi birorta manbaga mos kelmasligini ko‘rsatadi, ya’ni idishlar boshqa joyda yasalgan. Bu uning fikrini zaiflashtiradi.

A bu joyda sopol yasalganini ko‘rsatadi, bu Tursunovni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. B idishlarni mahalliy sopol bilan bog‘laydi, bu ham uni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. D idishlar qayerda topilganini aytadi, qayerda yasalganini emas.

passage: Songbirds of one species sing at a higher pitch in cities than in forests. Biologist Laylo Xasanova proposes that city birds raise their pitch so that their songs can be heard above the low rumble of traffic. Another possible explanation is that city birds of the species are simply smaller, and smaller birds naturally produce higher-pitched songs.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Xasanova's explanation over the alternative explanation?
option_a: City birds of the species weigh slightly less, on average, than forest birds of the species.
option_b: Individual city birds sang at a higher pitch on weekday mornings, when traffic was heavy, than on holiday mornings, when traffic was light.
option_c: Both city birds and forest birds of the species sing most often in the early morning.
option_d: City birds of the species sing at a higher pitch than forest birds of the same species do.
explanation_en:
To favor Xasanova's explanation, a finding should link pitch to traffic noise in a way that body size cannot explain. In Choice B, the same birds, whose size does not change from day to day, sing higher when traffic is heavy. That points to noise, not size.

Choice A shows that city birds are smaller, which supports the alternative explanation. Choice C describes when the birds sing, which does not distinguish the explanations. Choice D simply restates the observation that both explanations are trying to account for.
explanation_uz:
Xasanovaning tushuntirishini afzal ko‘rsatish uchun topilma ovoz balandligini tana o‘lchami bilan izohlab bo‘lmaydigan tarzda transport shovqiniga bog‘lashi kerak. B javobda o‘sha qushlarning o‘zi — ularning o‘lchami kundan kunga o‘zgarmaydi — transport ko‘p bo‘lganda balandroq kuylaydi. Bu o‘lchamga emas, shovqinga ishora qiladi.

A shahar qushlari kichikroq ekanini ko‘rsatadi, bu muqobil tushuntirishni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. C qushlar qachon kuylashini tasvirlaydi va tushuntirishlarni farqlamaydi. D ikkala tushuntirish izohlamoqchi bo‘lgan kuzatuvning o‘zini takrorlaydi xolos.

passage: In an essay about city life, writer Jamshid Ahmedov argues that walking reveals details of a city that are invisible from a car, even along routes a person already knows well.
stem: Which quotation from Ahmedov's essay most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “On foot, I noticed for the first time the small blue tiles set into the doorway of a bakery I had driven past every day for six years.”
option_b: “On my first walk through an unfamiliar neighborhood, I came across a tiny garden hidden behind a crumbling wall.”
option_c: “Cars allow residents of large cities to reach jobs and schools that are far from their homes.”
option_d: “The city's oldest streets were laid out long before anyone imagined there would be cars.”
explanation_en:
The claim has two parts: walking reveals details a driver misses, and this happens even on familiar routes. Choice A shows both: on foot, Ahmedov notices tiles on a bakery he had driven past daily for six years.

Choice B shows a discovery made on foot, but in an unfamiliar neighborhood, so it misses the "familiar routes" part of the claim. Choice C describes an advantage of cars. Choice D is a historical fact about the streets and says nothing about what walkers notice.
explanation_uz:
Da’vo ikki qismdan iborat: piyoda yurish haydovchi ko‘rmaydigan tafsilotlarni ochadi va bu hatto tanish yo‘llarda ham yuz beradi. A javob ikkalasini ko‘rsatadi: piyoda yurib, Ahmedov olti yil davomida har kuni mashinada o‘tgan novvoyxona eshigidagi koshinlarni payqaydi.

B piyoda qilingan kashfiyotni ko‘rsatadi, lekin notanish mahallada, shuning uchun da’voning "tanish yo‘llar" qismiga mos kelmaydi. C mashinalarning afzalligini tasvirlaydi. D ko‘chalar haqidagi tarixiy ma’lumot, piyodalar nimani payqashi haqida hech narsa demaydi.

passage: Linguist Otabek Nurmatov hypothesizes that children who regularly use two languages become better at ignoring distractions, because they constantly practice holding back the language they are not using at the moment. If this is right, the advantage should be greatest for children who switch between their languages most often.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Nurmatov's hypothesis?
option_a: Bilingual children in the study learned to read at about the same age as monolingual children did.
option_b: Most bilingual children in the study spoke one language at home and the other at school.
option_c: On a vocabulary test in their main language, monolingual children scored slightly higher than bilingual children.
option_d: Bilingual children made fewer errors than monolingual children of the same age on a task that required ignoring distracting sounds, and the bilingual children who switched languages most often during a typical day made the fewest errors of all.
explanation_en:
Nurmatov predicts that bilingual children are better at ignoring distractions and that frequent switching makes the advantage larger. Choice D confirms both predictions: bilingual children made fewer errors, and the most frequent switchers made the fewest.

Choice A compares reading age, not the ability to ignore distractions. Choice B describes when the children use each language but reports no test result. Choice C concerns vocabulary, a different skill from the one the hypothesis is about.
explanation_uz:
Nurmatovning taxminicha, ikki tilli bolalar chalg‘ituvchi narsalarga e’tibor bermaslikda ustunroq va tillarni tez-tez almashtirish bu ustunlikni kuchaytiradi. D javob ikkala taxminni tasdiqlaydi: ikki tilli bolalar kamroq xato qilgan, tillarni eng ko‘p almashtirganlar esa eng kam xato qilgan.

A chalg‘ituvchilarni e’tiborsiz qoldirish qobiliyatini emas, o‘qishni o‘rganish yoshini solishtiradi. B bolalar har bir tildan qachon foydalanishini tasvirlaydi, lekin test natijasini bermaydi. C lug‘at boyligi haqida, bu farazdagi ko‘nikmadan boshqa ko‘nikma.

passage: Chemist Sevara Islomova has developed a new coating for steel bridges. In tests, coated steel rusted far less than uncoated steel. Islomova claims that the coating works by forming a barrier that keeps moisture from ever reaching the surface of the metal.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Islomova's claim?
option_a: Coated steel samples rusted far less than uncoated samples during a year of outdoor exposure.
option_b: Water droplets bead up and roll off the coating's surface instead of soaking in.
option_c: Applying the coating costs more than applying the paint currently used on most bridges.
option_d: Moisture sensors placed beneath the coating showed water reaching the steel surface within hours, yet the coated steel still did not rust.
explanation_en:
Islomova's claim is about how the coating works: by keeping moisture away from the metal. Choice D shows that moisture does reach the metal, yet the steel still does not rust, so the coating must protect the steel in some other way. This weakens her claim about the mechanism.

Choice A shows that the coating prevents rust, which fits her claim. Choice B suggests the coating repels water, which also fits. Choice C is about cost, not about how the coating works.
explanation_uz:
Islomovaning da’vosi qoplama qanday ishlashi haqida: u namlikni metallga yetkazmaydi. D javob namlik metallga yetib borishini, lekin po‘lat baribir zanglamasligini ko‘rsatadi, demak qoplama boshqa yo‘l bilan himoya qiladi. Bu uning mexanizm haqidagi da’vosini zaiflashtiradi.

A qoplama zangdan saqlashini ko‘rsatadi, bu da’voga mos. B qoplama suvni itarishini ko‘rsatadi, bu ham mos. C qoplama qanday ishlashi haqida emas, narxi haqida.

passage: Excavations at a settlement that was occupied about 900 years ago have revealed large, richly furnished houses. Historian Akmal Yusupov argues that the settlement grew wealthy mainly by making glass and trading it over long distances, rather than by farming.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Yusupov's argument?
option_a: The settlement's fields were watered by an extensive network of canals.
option_b: Houses in the wealthiest part of the settlement were larger than houses elsewhere in it.
option_c: Glass workshops, with furnaces and heaps of glass waste, make up nearly a third of the buildings excavated, and pieces of the settlement's distinctive blue glass have been found at sites hundreds of kilometers away.
option_d: Coins from distant regions were found at the settlement, but in smaller numbers than at most trading towns of the period.
explanation_en:
Yusupov argues that glassmaking and long-distance trade, not farming, made the settlement rich. Choice C supports both parts: glass production was a major activity, and the settlement's glass reached distant places.

Choice A points to large-scale farming, which, if anything, favors the explanation Yusupov rejects. Choice B shows differences in wealth inside the settlement but not where the wealth came from. Choice D suggests that trade was less important than at other trading towns, which works against his argument.
explanation_uz:
Yusupovning fikricha, aholi punktini dehqonchilik emas, shisha ishlab chiqarish va uzoq masofali savdo boyitgan. C javob ikkala qismni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi: shisha ishlab chiqarish asosiy faoliyat bo‘lgan va bu yerning shishasi uzoq joylarga yetib borgan.

A keng ko‘lamli dehqonchilikka ishora qiladi, bu Yusupov rad etgan tushuntirishni quvvatlaydi. B aholi punkti ichidagi boylik farqini ko‘rsatadi, lekin boylik qayerdan kelganini emas. D savdo boshqa savdo shaharlaridagidan kamroq ahamiyatga ega bo‘lganini ko‘rsatadi, bu uning fikriga qarshi ishlaydi.

passage: *The Clockmaker's Grandson* is a novel. In the novel, the narrator suggests that his grandfather, although he repaired clocks for a living, cared very little about being on time himself.
stem: Which quotation from *The Clockmaker's Grandson* most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “Customers came from every corner of the city to bring Grandfather their broken clocks.”
option_b: “Grandfather's workshop was so full of ticking that I could hardly hear myself think.”
option_c: “Grandfather could make any stopped watch tick again within minutes, yet he arrived at my sister's wedding after the last plates had been cleared away.”
option_d: “Every morning at exactly seven, Grandfather unlocked the shop and wound the great clock in the window.”
explanation_en:
The claim contrasts the grandfather's skill with clocks and his own lateness. Choice C presents both: he can fix any watch in minutes, yet he arrives at a wedding after the meal is over.

Choice A shows his skill as a clockmaker but not his lateness. Choice B describes the noise of the workshop. Choice D shows him as punctual, which contradicts the claim.
explanation_uz:
Da’vo bobosining soatsozlikdagi mahoratini va o‘zining kechikishini qarama-qarshi qo‘yadi. C javob ikkalasini ko‘rsatadi: u har qanday soatni bir necha daqiqada tuzatadi, lekin to‘yga dasturxon yig‘ishtirilgandan keyin keladi.

A uning mahoratini ko‘rsatadi, lekin kechikishini emas. B ustaxonadagi shovqinni tasvirlaydi. D uni vaqtga juda rioya qiluvchi qilib ko‘rsatadi, bu da’voga zid.

passage: Psychologist Madina Qodirova hypothesizes that people recall information better when they are tested in the same place where they learned it, because features of the surroundings act as reminders. To test this idea, she had volunteers memorize a list of words in one of two rooms that differed in color, furniture, and smell, and later tested their memory.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Qodirova's hypothesis?
option_a: Volunteers tested in the quieter of the two rooms recalled more words than volunteers tested in the noisier room, regardless of where they had studied.
option_b: Volunteers who studied the list for twenty minutes recalled more words than volunteers who studied it for ten minutes.
option_c: Volunteers rated both rooms as equally comfortable places to study.
option_d: Volunteers who studied and were tested in the same room recalled more words than volunteers who studied in one room and were tested in the other.
explanation_en:
The hypothesis is about a match between the place of learning and the place of testing. Choice D compares volunteers whose rooms matched with volunteers whose rooms did not, and finds better recall with a match, directly supporting the hypothesis.

Choice A shows an effect of noise in the testing room "regardless of where they had studied," so it is not about a match between rooms. Choice B shows an effect of study time. Choice C reports opinions about comfort, not memory.
explanation_uz:
Faraz o‘rganilgan joy bilan sinov o‘tkazilgan joyning mos kelishi haqida. D javob xonalari mos kelgan va mos kelmagan ko‘ngillilarni solishtiradi va mos kelganda eslash yaxshiroq ekanini ko‘rsatadi; bu farazni bevosita qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi.

A "qayerda o‘qiganidan qat’i nazar" sinov xonasidagi shovqin ta’sirini ko‘rsatadi, ya’ni xonalarning mos kelishi haqida emas. B o‘qish vaqtining ta’sirini ko‘rsatadi. C xotira haqida emas, qulaylik haqidagi fikrlarni beradi.

passage: Astronomers recently discovered a small asteroid whose orbit lies close to that of a much larger asteroid known as Asteroid K. Astronomer Diyora Mirzayeva hypothesizes that the small asteroid is a fragment that broke off Asteroid K during a collision long ago.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Mirzayeva's hypothesis?
option_a: The small asteroid's orbit is tilted at almost the same angle as Asteroid K's orbit.
option_b: Analysis of reflected sunlight shows that the minerals on the small asteroid's surface are very different from those on Asteroid K's surface.
option_c: The small asteroid is less than one-hundredth the width of Asteroid K.
option_d: The small asteroid spins once every six hours, faster than Asteroid K does.
explanation_en:
A fragment of Asteroid K should be made of the same materials as Asteroid K. Choice B shows that the two asteroids have very different surface minerals, which makes it less likely that the small one came from Asteroid K. This weakens the hypothesis.

Choice A shows another similarity between the orbits, which supports the hypothesis. Choice C is expected, since a fragment would be much smaller than its parent. Choice D gives a difference in spin, but a broken-off fragment could easily spin at a different rate, so this does not weaken the hypothesis.
explanation_uz:
K asteroidining bo‘lagi K asteroidi bilan bir xil moddalardan iborat bo‘lishi kerak. B javob ikki asteroidning sirtidagi minerallar juda farq qilishini ko‘rsatadi, demak kichik asteroid K dan ajralib chiqqan bo‘lishi ehtimoli kamroq. Bu farazni zaiflashtiradi.

A orbitalar orasidagi yana bir o‘xshashlikni ko‘rsatadi, bu farazni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. C kutilgan holat, chunki bo‘lak o‘z manbasidan ancha kichik bo‘ladi. D aylanish tezligidagi farqni beradi, lekin ajralib chiqqan bo‘lak boshqa tezlikda aylanishi oddiy hol, shuning uchun bu farazni zaiflashtirmaydi.

passage: *A Season of Lanterns* is a novel. In the novel, the narrator suggests that she understood the sacrifices her mother had made for the family only after she began supporting herself as an adult.
stem: Which quotation from *A Season of Lanterns* most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “As a child, I was embarrassed that Mother never bought herself new shoes, and once I even told her so.”
option_b: “It was not until I had my own small apartment, and my own empty purse at the end of each month, that I understood why Mother had always served herself last.”
option_c: “Mother worked at the textile mill for twenty-two years and was never once late for her shift.”
option_d: “Now that I am grown, I visit Mother every Sunday and bring her the round bread she likes best.”
explanation_en:
The claim has three elements: a sacrifice by the mother, the narrator's understanding of it, and the timing of that understanding (only once she supported herself). Choice B includes all three: living on her own budget, the narrator finally understands why her mother "always served herself last."

Choice A mentions a sacrifice, but from the narrator's childhood, when she clearly did not yet understand it. Choice C shows the mother's hard work but not the narrator's later understanding. Choice D shows the adult narrator caring for her mother but says nothing about understanding her sacrifices.
explanation_uz:
Da’vo uch unsurdan iborat: onaning fidoyiligi, hikoyachining buni tushunishi va bu tushunish vaqti (faqat o‘zini o‘zi ta’minlay boshlaganda). B javobda uchalasi bor: o‘z byudjeti bilan yashay boshlagach, hikoyachi nihoyat onasi nega "doim o‘ziga oxirida suzganini" tushunadi.

A fidoyilikni eslatadi, ammo hikoyachi hali buni tushunmagan bolalik davridan. C onaning mehnatsevarligini ko‘rsatadi, hikoyachining keyingi tushunishini emas. D katta bo‘lgan hikoyachining onasiga g‘amxo‘rligini ko‘rsatadi, lekin uning fidoyiligini tushunish haqida hech narsa demaydi.

passage: Over the past twenty years, a small fish species has become much rarer in a mountain lake. Biologist Javlon Murodov attributes the decline to the lake's warming water, which holds less oxygen and, he argues, causes more of the fish's eggs to die. Other researchers note that a predatory trout species was introduced into the lake during the same period and blame the decline on the trout.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most strongly support Murodov's explanation rather than the alternative explanation?
option_a: Trout in the lake have been observed eating adults of the small fish species.
option_b: The lake's average summer water temperature has risen by about 2°C over the past twenty years.
option_c: In a nearby lake that has warmed by a similar amount but has never contained trout, the same small fish has declined at about the same rate.
option_d: During summer, both the small fish and the trout spend most of their time in the cooler water near the lake bottom.
explanation_en:
Because the warming and the arrival of trout happened at the same time, a finding that favors Murodov must separate the two. Choice C does so: in a lake that warmed similarly but has no trout, the fish declined just as fast, so warming alone can account for the decline.

Choice A supports the trout explanation. Choice B confirms that the lake warmed, but the trout arrived during the same period, so this finding cannot tell the explanations apart. Choice D shows that the two species use the same part of the lake, which, if anything, makes predation by trout more plausible.
explanation_uz:
Isish va gulmohilarning paydo bo‘lishi bir vaqtda sodir bo‘lgani uchun Murodovni afzal ko‘rsatadigan topilma bu ikkisini ajratishi kerak. C javob shuni qiladi: xuddi shunday isigan, lekin gulmohi bo‘lmagan ko‘lda ham baliq shunday tez kamaygan, demak isishning o‘zi kamayishni tushuntira oladi.

A gulmohi tushuntirishini qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. B ko‘l isiganini tasdiqlaydi, lekin gulmohilar ham aynan shu davrda paydo bo‘lgan, shuning uchun bu topilma tushuntirishlarni ajrata olmaydi. D ikki tur ko‘lning bir qismidan foydalanishini ko‘rsatadi, bu esa gulmohilarning ovlashini yanada ehtimolliroq qiladi.

passage: After a city made admission to its art museum free, yearly attendance at the museum rose by 40 percent. Economist Nilufar Saidova concludes that the admission fee had been keeping lower-income residents away from the museum, and that removing the fee brought many of them in for the first time.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Saidova's conclusion?
option_a: Before the change, many lower-income residents told surveyors that the admission fee was more than they could afford.
option_b: Attendance at the city's history museum, which had always been free, stayed the same during the period.
option_c: Sales at the museum's café and gift shop rose by roughly the same percentage as attendance did.
option_d: Visitor surveys showed that the share of visitors from lower-income households was the same before and after the change, and that most of the increase came from people who had visited before and now came more often.
explanation_en:
Saidova concludes not just that attendance rose but that the rise came from lower-income residents visiting for the first time. Choice D contradicts that specific conclusion: the share of lower-income visitors did not change, and the extra visits came mainly from returning visitors.

Choice A suggests the fee was a barrier for lower-income residents, which supports Saidova. Choice B suggests that the rise was caused by the free admission rather than by a general trend, which also fits her conclusion. Choice C simply reflects the larger number of visitors and says nothing about who they were.
explanation_uz:
Saidova faqat tashrif buyuruvchilar ko‘paydi demayapti, balki o‘sish kam daromadli aholining birinchi marta kelishi hisobiga bo‘lgan, deb xulosa qiladi. D javob aynan shu xulosaga zid: kam daromadli tashrif buyuruvchilar ulushi o‘zgarmagan, qo‘shimcha tashriflar esa asosan avval kelgan odamlardan bo‘lgan.

A to‘lov kam daromadli aholi uchun to‘siq bo‘lganini ko‘rsatadi, bu Saidovani qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. B o‘sishga umumiy tendensiya emas, bepul kirish sabab bo‘lganini ko‘rsatadi, bu ham uning xulosasiga mos. C shunchaki tashrif buyuruvchilar soni ko‘payganini aks ettiradi va ular kimligi haqida hech narsa demaydi.

passage: At a fossil site, dozens of footprints show that several small dinosaurs of the same species crossed what was once a mudflat. Paleontologist Sardor Ibragimov argues that the animals crossed the mudflat together as a group, rather than one at a time over a period of days or weeks.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ibragimov's argument?
option_a: The footprints were made by animals of several different sizes.
option_b: The mudflat was later buried under a thick layer of volcanic ash, which preserved the footprints.
option_c: Footprints of the same species have been found at several other sites in the region.
option_d: All the footprints are equally deep and equally sharp, indicating that the mud was in the same condition when each was made, and no footprint crosses over another.
explanation_en:
To show that the animals crossed together, a finding must show that the footprints were made at the same time. Choice D does this: mud changes as it dries, so identical depth and sharpness suggest the prints were made under the same conditions, and the lack of overlapping prints fits animals walking side by side.

Choice A shows animals of different sizes, which could cross together or separately. Choice B explains how the prints were preserved, not when they were made. Choice C concerns other sites and says nothing about whether these animals crossed together.
explanation_uz:
Hayvonlar birga o‘tganini ko‘rsatish uchun topilma izlar bir vaqtda qoldirilganini ko‘rsatishi kerak. D javob shuni qiladi: loy qurigan sari o‘zgaradi, shuning uchun izlarning bir xil chuqurlik va aniqlikda bo‘lishi ular bir xil sharoitda qoldirilganini bildiradi, izlarning bir-birini kesib o‘tmasligi esa yonma-yon yurgan hayvonlarga mos keladi.

A turli o‘lchamdagi hayvonlarni ko‘rsatadi, ular birga ham, alohida ham o‘tishi mumkin. B izlar qanday saqlanganini tushuntiradi, qachon qoldirilganini emas. C boshqa joylar haqida va bu hayvonlar birga o‘tganmi-yo‘qmi, buni aytmaydi.

passage: In an essay on translation, critic Zuhra Karimova argues that a good translation of a poem must sometimes depart from the literal meaning of the original in order to preserve the effect the poem has on its readers.
stem: Which quotation from Karimova's essay most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “A translator who changes a poem's meaning betrays both the poet and the reader, who trusts that every word is the poet's own.”
option_b: “Translating poetry is harder than translating prose, because a poem depends so heavily on sound and rhythm.”
option_c: “When a line makes its readers laugh through a pun that has no equivalent in English, the faithful translator must invent a new pun, even if that means abandoning the words the poet actually wrote.”
option_d: “The best translators of poetry are usually poets themselves, with a trained ear for the music of language.”
explanation_en:
Karimova's claim is that a translator should sometimes give up literal meaning to keep a poem's effect. Choice C gives a concrete case: to keep a line funny, the translator must invent a new pun and abandon the poet's actual words.

Choice A argues the opposite, that changing the meaning is a betrayal. Choice B explains why poetry is hard to translate but does not say that meaning should be sacrificed for effect. Choice D describes who makes good translators, not what a good translation must do.
explanation_uz:
Karimovaning da’vosicha, tarjimon she’rning ta’sirini saqlash uchun ba’zan so‘zma-so‘z ma’nodan voz kechishi kerak. C javob aniq misol beradi: satrning kulgili ekanini saqlash uchun tarjimon yangi so‘z o‘yinini o‘ylab topishi va shoirning asl so‘zlaridan voz kechishi kerak.

A buning teskarisini, ya’ni ma’noni o‘zgartirish xiyonat ekanini ta’kidlaydi. B she’rni tarjima qilish nega qiyinligini tushuntiradi, lekin ta’sir uchun ma’nodan voz kechish kerakligini aytmaydi. D yaxshi tarjima nima qilishi kerakligini emas, kim yaxshi tarjimon bo‘lishini tasvirlaydi.

passage: In a forest she studies, ecologist Rayhona Hamroyeva has observed that a species of squirrel buries many more acorns near the bases of large oak trees than in open areas. She hypothesizes that the squirrels choose these spots because the large trees serve as landmarks that help the squirrels find their buried acorns again later.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Hamroyeva's hypothesis?
option_a: When researchers tracked buried acorns, the squirrels recovered acorns buried near large oaks no more often than acorns buried in open ground with no landmarks nearby.
option_b: The squirrels also bury many acorns next to large boulders and fallen logs.
option_c: The squirrels never recovered some of the acorns buried near large oaks, and some of those acorns later sprouted into seedlings.
option_d: Older squirrels buried a greater share of their acorns near large oaks than younger squirrels did.
explanation_en:
If large trees helped the squirrels find their acorns, acorns buried near those trees should be recovered more often. Choice A shows that they were recovered no more often than acorns buried far from any landmark, which weakens the hypothesis.

Choice B shows the squirrels using other landmarks too, which is consistent with the hypothesis. Choice C is partly tempting, but some unrecovered acorns are expected under any explanation, and the choice gives no comparison with acorns buried elsewhere. Choice D may suggest that the behavior is learned, which fits the hypothesis rather than weakening it.
explanation_uz:
Agar katta daraxtlar olmaxonlarga yong‘oqlarini topishga yordam bersa, bu daraxtlar yonida ko‘milgan yong‘oqlar ko‘proq topilishi kerak. A javob ular hech qanday mo‘ljal bo‘lmagan ochiq joyda ko‘milganlardan ko‘proq topilmaganini ko‘rsatadi, bu farazni zaiflashtiradi.

B olmaxonlar boshqa mo‘ljallardan ham foydalanishini ko‘rsatadi, bu farazga mos. C jozibali tuyuladi, ammo har qanday tushuntirishda ham ba’zi yong‘oqlar topilmay qolishi kutiladi va bu javob boshqa joylarda ko‘milgan yong‘oqlar bilan solishtirish bermaydi. D bu xatti-harakat o‘rganilgan ekaniga ishora qilishi mumkin, bu farazni zaiflashtirmaydi, unga mos keladi.

passage: “Inventory” is a poem. In the poem, the speaker sorts through her late grandmother's belongings and suggests that the objects she treasures most would be worth almost nothing to anyone else.
stem: Which quotation from “Inventory” most effectively illustrates the claim?
option_a: “The silver spoons we sent to the appraiser / came back with prices none of us expected.”
option_b: “A thimble dented by a thousand hems, / a chipped blue cup: I'd give the house for these, / though any stranger would toss them in a bin.”
option_c: “I fold her scarves and lay them in a box, / the way she folded mine each end of winter.”
option_d: “Each thing she kept, she kept for some good reason, / though half those reasons went with her to the grave.”
explanation_en:
The claim has two parts: the speaker treasures certain objects, and those objects would mean almost nothing to others. Choice B contains both: she would "give the house" for a dented thimble and a chipped cup, though "any stranger would toss them in a bin."

Choice A is about objects whose value to others surprised the family, the reverse of the claim. Choice C shows tender memory but does not compare the speaker's view of the scarves with anyone else's. Choice D suggests that the objects' meaning is partly lost, but it does not show the speaker treasuring them or contrast her view with others'.
explanation_uz:
Da’vo ikki qismdan iborat: so‘zlovchi ba’zi narsalarni juda qadrlaydi va bu narsalar boshqalar uchun deyarli qadrsiz. B javobda ikkalasi bor: u ezilgan angishvona va darz ketgan kosa uchun "uyni berishga" tayyor, garchi "har qanday begona ularni axlatga tashlashi" mumkin bo‘lsa ham.

A boshqalar uchun qiymati oilani hayratga solgan narsalar haqida, bu da’voning teskarisi. C iliq xotirani ko‘rsatadi, lekin so‘zlovchining ro‘mollarga qarashini boshqalarnikiga solishtirmaydi. D narsalarning ma’nosi qisman yo‘qolganiga ishora qiladi, lekin so‘zlovchi ularni qadrlashini ko‘rsatmaydi va uning qarashini boshqalarnikiga qarama-qarshi qo‘ymaydi.

passage: Concrete in cold climates often cracks as water inside it repeatedly freezes and thaws. Engineer Kamron Rasulov hypothesizes that adding finely ground rice husk ash to a standard concrete mixture makes the concrete more resistant to this kind of cracking.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Rasulov's hypothesis?
option_a: Concrete blocks containing the ash and otherwise identical blocks without it were frozen and thawed 300 times, and the blocks with the ash developed far fewer cracks.
option_b: Before any freezing, blocks containing the ash withstood heavier loads than blocks without it.
option_c: Blocks containing the ash developed fewer cracks after 300 freeze-thaw cycles than ordinary blocks did after only 100 cycles in an earlier, unrelated study.
option_d: During freeze-thaw testing, blocks containing a small amount of the ash cracked less than blocks containing a large amount of it.
explanation_en:
To support the hypothesis, a finding must compare concrete with and without the ash under the same freeze-thaw conditions. Choice A does exactly that, and the blocks with ash cracked far less.

Choice B concerns strength before freezing, a different property from resistance to freeze-thaw cracking. Choice C compares results from two different studies, which may have used different concrete, cycles, and conditions, so the comparison is not reliable. Choice D compares two amounts of ash but includes no concrete without ash, so it cannot show that adding ash helps.

B muzlashdan oldingi mustahkamlik haqida, bu muzlash-erishdan yorilishga chidamlilikdan boshqa xususiyat. C ikki turli tadqiqot natijalarini solishtiradi, ularda beton, sikllar va sharoit turlicha bo‘lishi mumkin, shuning uchun bu solishtirish ishonchli emas. D kulning ikki miqdorini solishtiradi, lekin kulsiz beton yo‘q, shuning uchun kul qo‘shish foyda berishini ko‘rsata olmaydi.
